headline: President Bush ends a national emergency that the U.S. had declared concerning the West African countries of Sierra Leone and Liberia.
what_it_does: This order ends a national emergency that the U.S. government had earlier declared regarding Sierra Leone and Liberia. National emergencies like this are usually used to put economic restrictions, such as trade or import limits, on certain countries. Ending the emergency generally means the rules that depended on it no longer apply. The title does not say which specific restrictions were lifted.

who_it_affects.group: U.S. businesses and importers dealing with Sierra Leone or Liberia
who_it_affects.how: Restrictions on trade tied to this emergency would no longer apply to them.

who_it_affects.group: People and businesses in Sierra Leone and Liberia
who_it_affects.how: U.S. limits connected to this emergency would be lifted for them.

when_it_takes_effect: Signed January 15, 2004; the exact effective date is not given in the title.
